subject: Evaluating Redwood for clinical summarization — demo request
messages:
From: Megan Lowe <megan@sparkline.health>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluating Redwood for clinical summarization — demo request

Hi Monica,

I signed up through the self-serve flow this morning — Sparkline Health is exploring Redwood to power a clinical summarization feature in our clinician workflow. We have a small pilot (~5 clinics) that needs accurate, concise patient summaries extracted from visit notes and structured EHR fields.

Topline:
- Primary use case: condense latest visit + meds + outstanding tasks into a 2–3 sentence summary for clinicians
- Expected pilot load: ~1k requests/day, peak ~3k/day; average request ~400–800 tokens; concurrency low initially (2–5)
- Timeline: pilot in 6–8 weeks, production later in Q4 if results look good

Can someone run a short demo and share whether Redwood can meet latency and privacy expectations (HIPAA / SOC2)? I attached a brief requirements doc.

Thanks,
Megan Lowe
Product Lead, Sparkline Health
megan@sparkline.health
(attachment: sparkline_requirements.pdf)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood for clinical summarization — demo request

Hi Megan — welcome and thanks for the details, this is exactly the kind of pilot we love to help with. A couple quick clarifying questions so we make the demo actionable: 

1) Input shape: are you sending an entire visit note + structured fields in one request, or will you send streaming updates (e.g., notes + meds separately)?
2) Typical tokens per request (best guess) and max tokens you might include in the pilot?
3) Latency SLO for an interactive clinician flow (95th pct target)?
4) Any strict hosting requirement — hosted API is fastest, but we also support private/VPC for regulated data. Will you need an on-prem or VPC deployment for the pilot?
5) Are there specific evaluation metrics you’ll use (precision of extracted diagnoses, hallucination tolerance, etc.)?

Proposed demo agenda (30–40m):
- 5m intro + goals
- 10m model selection & perf profile (latency/cost tradeoffs)
- 15m runthrough: sample input -> summary -> edit loop + Q&A
- Next steps: pilot scope & timeline

I have availability (PDT): Tue Jun 30 — 9:00am, 11:30am, 3:00pm. If none of those work I can propose other times — feel free to send over a calendar link.

I’ll loop in Ben (solutions engineer) to cover perf and integration patterns.

Best,
Monica Patel
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica@redwoodinference.com

From: Megan Lowe <megan@sparkline.health>

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood for clinical summarization — demo request

Hi Monica — thanks for the quick reply and the proposed slots. Answers below and I attached a small redacted sample set for the demo.

Answers to your Qs:
- Input shape: we’ll send a single payload for the demo with the latest visit note plus a small set of structured fields (meds, vitals). In production we might experiment with delta updates but pilot will be single-payload.
- Tokens: average ~550 tokens, 95th ~1,200 tokens (some notes can be long)
- Latency SLO: 95th under 800ms would be ideal for a clinician-facing result; for pilot we can tolerate up to 1.5s if justified by quality
- Hosting: we need SOC2 and HIPAA controls. For the pilot we prefer a VPC/private deployment or hosted with a BAA — open to options.
- Evaluation metrics: clinical accuracy (no hallucinated meds/diagnoses), brevity, and clinician acceptance score (NPS-style).

Attachment: redacted_patient_snippets.csv (sample input, PHI removed)

Regarding the demo time: the Tue times overlap with an internal leadership sync. Can we move to Wed Jul 1? My availability (PDT): Wed Jul 1 — 10:30am, 2:00pm. Either works, and we’d like a recording if possible.

Thanks,
Megan
Product Lead, Sparkline Health
(attachment: redacted_patient_snippets.csv)
